figures.caption: TABLE I: Performance of different DDR (latency 100 ns) and HBS set ups without and with restricted DDR-HBS traffic.

Fig. 3: Achieved TPS for the three different configurations of DDR: bandwidth set at I) LPDDR6, II) 3x LPDDR6, III) 3x LPDDR6 with Q, K, V cached at DDR. HBS bandwidth and latency are fixed at 512 GB/s and 10 us. The data are for three different context windows.

Fig. 1: TPS as a function of HBS bandwidth and latency when DDR bandwidth is set at (a) 173 GB/s (LPDDR6), (b) 520 GB/s (3x stacked LPDDR6). The data are for LLaVa1.5-13B with single precision. DDR latency is fixed at 100 ns.

Fig. 2: (a) TPS as a function of HBS bandwidth when latency is fixed at 10 µs for three different configurations of DDR: with I) LPDDR6, II) 3x LPDDR6 – in both of these cases Q, K, V, activations and weights are in HBS, III) 3x LPDDR6 and the attention traffic is restricted to DDR. (b) Time (per layer) spent in different GEMM operations (see Sec. II) for two different HBS latencies while bandwidth is fixed at 512 GB/s. The ones involved in self-attention are patterned.

Fig. 4: Performance implications of QKV chiplet for Llama3.2-1B model while the bandwidth of the chiplet is varied for different latency configurations of DDR with the bandwidth fixed at 173 GB/s. The solid bars indicate the baseline performance with no chiplet configuration.
